title: Particle verbs II: split, fused and turned into adjectives
goal: Recognize the two lives of a Swedish particle verb — split in speech (*lämna in*), fused in official writing (*inlämna*) — and turn particle verbs into participles like *avstängd* and *uppskriven*.
bekal: you can build participles from particle verbs and make them agree: *avstängd, avstängt, avstängda*
you can tell when a fused verb means the same thing in a formal voice (*lämna in* / *inlämna*) and when it means something else (*gå under* / *undergå*)
you can unpack a landlord's or an authority's letter into everyday Swedish
wave: Go back to Svenska 102, Unit 3: say every particle verb in the dialogue aloud with the stress on the particle (*stänga AV*, *ta på sig*), then turn five of them into participles from this unit: *stänga av* → *avstängd*, *sätta på* → *påsatt*.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Nätet är avstängt
dialogs.intro: Dian arrives at the office on a Monday morning, opens her laptop — and nothing happens. Mattias and Leila are already sitting at their desks with coffee and no internet.

lines.text: God morgon! Varför är nätet avstängt?
lines.id: Good morning! Why is the network down?
lines.literal: good morning! why is net-the off-shut?

lines.speaker: Mattias:
lines.text: IT stängde av det i natt. De byter ut alla servrar.
lines.id: IT shut it off last night. They're replacing all the servers.
lines.literal: IT shut off it in night. they change out all servers.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Hela dagen? Jag har ett kundmöte klockan tio.
lines.id: All day? I have a client meeting at ten.

lines.text: Mötet är inställt. Kunden ställde in det sent i går kväll.

lines.text: Att projektet går igenom en omstart. Karin skriver alltid som en myndighet.

lines.text: Det är lugnt. Dian, kan du ta upp dina skisser på mötet efter lunch? Jag är upptagen hela förmiddagen.

lines.text: Absolut. Men utan nätet blir det svårt — alla filer ligger i molnet.

notes: **Avstängt** (**AHV-stengt**) is the participle of *stänga av* (to turn off). When a particle verb becomes a participle, the particle **jumps to the front and fuses** with the verb: *stänga av* → *avstängd*. It then agrees like any adjective — *nätet* is an *ett*-word, so *avstängt*. The stress stays where it was: on the particle.

**IT stängde av det** — in the active verb the particle stays separate, and it comes **before** the object, even when the object is a small pronoun. English says "shut **it** off"; Swedish says *stängde **av det***, *stäng **av den***, *skriv **upp det***. Never *stängde det av*.

**Mötet är inställt** — *ställa in* (**STEL-lah IN**) means "to cancel", and its participle *inställd/inställt/inställda* is everywhere in Swedish life: the word **INSTÄLLT** in red on a station departure board is something every commuter in Sweden has learned to dread.

**Jag har skrivit upp** / **allt står uppskrivet** — the perfect tense keeps the particle separate (*har skrivit upp*); only the participle fuses (*uppskrivet*). *Står* + participle describes the result, as English "is written": *Det står uppskrivet på tavlan* = It's written up on the board.

**Genomgår** vs **går igenom** — the same two pieces in two orders. The fused *genomgå* (**YEH-nom-goh**) means "to undergo" and belongs to formal writing; the split *gå igenom* is everyday "go through, review". Official Swedish loves fused verbs, which is exactly what Mattias is teasing Karin about. A *myndighet* (**MÜN-dee-het**) is a government agency.

**Ta upp** / **upptagen** — *ta upp* means "to pick up" or "to bring up (a topic)". Its fused relative *uppta* gives the participle *upptagen* (**ÜP-tah-gen**), "busy, occupied": *Jag är upptagen*, *Det är upptaget* (the line is busy, the toilet is occupied).

grammars.title: Participles of particle verbs
body: Recipe: take the past participle of the verb, put the particle in front, write it as one word, and make it agree with the noun (*en* / *ett* / plural). The perfect tense (*har stängt av*) and the s-passive (*stängs av*) keep the particle separate — only the participle fuses.
after: The endings follow the verb's own family: *-d/-t/-da* (*avstängd*), *-en/-et/-na* for strong verbs (*uppskriven*, *påslagen*), *-t/-t/-ta* after voiceless consonants (*upplåst*).

Present participles fuse in exactly the same way: *gå på* → ***pågående*** (ongoing), *komma in* → ***inkommande*** (incoming), *gå ut* → ***utgående*** (outgoing). You will see these on phones and in news: *ett inkommande samtal*, *en pågående utredning*. Participles used as adjectives get a unit of their own: Unit 9.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Ett brev från hyresvärden
dialogs.intro: Evening in Majorna. Dian rents her room second-hand (*i andra hand*) from Hanna, who holds the contract but is working in Berlin for a year. A letter from the landlord has arrived, and Dian calls Hanna to make sense of it.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Hej Hanna, det är Dian. Det har kommit ett brev från hyresvärden.
lines.id: Hi Hanna, it's Dian. A letter has come from the landlord.
lines.literal: hi Hanna, it is Dian. it has come a letter from landlord-the.

lines.speaker: Hanna:
lines.text: Åh nej. Vad står det?
lines.id: Oh no. What does it say?
lines.literal: oh no. what stands it?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: ”Under vecka 48 utförs stambyte i fastigheten.” Vad är ett stambyte?
lines.id: "During week 48, pipe replacement will be carried out in the building." What's a stambyte?
lines.literal: during week 48 out-carried stem-change in property-the. what is a stem-change?

lines.speaker: Hanna:
lines.text: De byter ut alla gamla rör. Badrummet kommer att vara avstängt i flera veckor.
lines.id: They replace all the old pipes. The bathroom will be out of use for several weeks.
lines.literal: they change out all old pipes. bathroom-the comes to be off-shut in several weeks.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Flera veckor?! Var ska jag duscha?
lines.id: Several weeks?! Where am I supposed to shower?
lines.literal: several weeks?! where shall I shower?

lines.speaker: Hanna:
lines.text: Det brukar stå en duschvagn på gården. Läs vidare.
lines.id: There's usually a shower trailer in the courtyard. Read on.
lines.literal: it uses-to stand a shower-wagon on yard-the. read further.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: ”Hyresgästen ombeds att tömma badrummet. Nycklar inlämnas till fastighetsskötaren senast den 20 november.”
lines.id: "The tenant is requested to empty the bathroom. Keys are to be handed in to the caretaker by November 20 at the latest."
lines.literal: tenant-the about-asked-is to empty bathroom-the. keys in-handed-are to property-caretaker-the latest the 20 November.

lines.speaker: Hanna:
lines.text: Alltså: töm badrummet och lämna in nyckeln till fastighetsskötaren.
lines.id: In other words: empty the bathroom and hand the key in to the caretaker.
lines.literal: so: empty bathroom-the and hand in key-the to property-caretaker-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Varför skriver de inte bara så?
lines.id: Why don't they just write that?
lines.literal: why write they not just so?

lines.speaker: Hanna:
lines.text: Hyresvärdar har sitt eget språk. Men ta det lugnt, jag ringer upp dem imorgon.
lines.id: Landlords have their own language. But relax, I'll give them a call tomorrow.
lines.literal: landlords have their own language. but take it calm, I ring up them tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Tack! Och om duschvagnen är upptagen när jag ska till jobbet?
lines.id: Thanks! And what if the shower trailer is occupied when I need to leave for work?
lines.literal: thanks! and if shower-wagon-the is up-taken when I shall to job-the?

lines.speaker: Hanna:
lines.text: Då får du gå upp tidigare. Eller duscha på gymmet!
lines.id: Then you'll have to get up earlier. Or shower at the gym!
lines.literal: then must you go up earlier. or shower on gym-the!

notes: **Utförs** — the s-passive of *utföra* (**ÜT-fö-rah**), "to carry out, to perform": *arbetet utförs* = the work is carried out. The split version *föra ut* means something else entirely — to carry something **out** of a place. This is the kind of pair where fusing changes the meaning.

**Ett stambyte** (**STAHM-bü-teh**) is a very Swedish ordeal: every fifty years or so, the main water and drain pipes (*stammar*) in an apartment building are replaced, and residents live for weeks without a bathroom. Shower trailers (*duschvagnar*) in the courtyard are part of the deal.

**Ombeds** — from *ombe* (**OM-beh**), the fused, formal form of *be om* (to ask for). *Hyresgästen ombeds att…* = The tenant is requested to… In speech, you would say *Vi ber dig att…* (we ask you to…). The fused verb plus s-passive is the trademark of official letters.

**Inlämnas** vs **lämna in** — here the meaning is identical; only the register changes. *Nycklar inlämnas* is notice-board Swedish, *lämna in nyckeln* is what a person says. Rule of thumb: when a fused form means the same as the split one, the fused form sounds formal or old-fashioned.
**Jag ringer upp dem** — *ringa upp* (**RING-ah ÜP**) is "to call someone up, to give someone a call"; stress on *upp*, as on every separable particle. *Dem* is pronounced **dom**, as always.

**Gå upp** means "to get up (out of bed)" — but its fused cousin *uppgå till* means "to amount to": *Kostnaden uppgår till 5 000 kronor.* Again: split = everyday and concrete, fused = formal and often abstract.

grammars.title: Split or fused? Same meaning or a new one?
body: Many particle verbs have a fused twin with the particle as a prefix. Some twins are just the formal version; others mean something different. When you meet a fused verb in a text, first try splitting it — if the result makes sense in context, the fused form is probably just the formal way of saying it.
after: Notice the pattern in the second group: the split verb is **concrete** (something physically sinks, is carried out, snaps), the fused verb is **abstract** (a project undergoes a change, a task is carried out, a speaker is interrupted). English shows the same thing with "to *set up* a tent" vs "to *upset* someone".
In the **present participle** and **past participle**, the verb is always fused, whatever the register: *en avbruten film* (from *avbryta*) but also *en avstängd telefon* (from *stänga av*).

sections.title: Reading formal Swedish: unpack the fused verbs

blocks.text: Letters from landlords, banks and authorities follow a recipe: a **fused verb** in the **s-passive**, often with no person in sight. To understand them, do what Hanna did — split the verb and turn the sentence into a request or a statement with a real subject:

head: Official text
Everyday Swedish
English
rows: Hand in the keys at reception.
Pay the rent by the last day of the month.
An outside company will do the work.

blocks.text: You will never need to *produce* the forms in the middle column in conversation — Swedes would find it odd. But you will read them every week, so recognizing them is a B1 skill.

blocks.title: One-word signs from particle verbs
items: **INSTÄLLT** — cancelled (*ställa in*) — on departure boards
**AVSTÄNGT** — closed off (*stänga av*) — on roads, escalators and machines
**UPPTAGET** — occupied, busy (*uppta*) — on toilet doors
**UTSÅLT** — sold out (*sälja ut*) — at concerts and in bakeries
**AVBOKAD** — cancelled booking (*boka av*) — in confirmation emails

blocks.text: Sweden's big cities have long housing queues: in Göteborg, as in Stockholm, people wait years for a first-hand lease. Most newcomers therefore rent **i andra hand** from someone who holds the contract, as Dian does from Hanna. It is legal, but the landlord usually has to approve it, so check before you sign anything.

The **tvättstuga** deserves a word of its own: the shared laundry room in the basement, booked in time slots on a list or a screen. Leaving it untidy, or using someone else's slot, is the classic source of neighborly war in Sweden.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 5
items: Combine this unit's particle verbs with the modal + perfect from Unit 5: *Jag borde ha skrivit upp numret.* *Hyresvärden kunde ha ringt upp tidigare.* *De måste ha stängt av vattnet.*
Make five sentences of your own. Check that the particle stays after the supine: *har skrivit **upp***, not *har uppskrivit*.
